usage: Common self-intro phrase; soften with 좀
성격 (personality) is the noun it pairs with most
I'd say I'm on the introverted side
-(으)ㄴ 편이다 hedges instead of stating it flatly
examples: 저는 내성적이라서 처음 보는 사람이랑 말하는 게 어려워요.
I'm introverted, so talking to people I'm meeting for the first time is hard.
Natural way to explain shyness at work or meetups
걔는 내성적이지만 친해지면 말이 엄청 많아.
He's introverted, but once you get close he talks a ton.
걔 = casual 'that person'; banmal among friends
내성적인 사람도 발표는 잘할 수 있어요.
Even introverted people can be good at presentations.
Reassuring tone, polite register
nuance: 내성적이다 is the neutral, textbook word for 'introverted' and is totally fine to say about yourself in interviews or intros. It describes drawing energy inward, not being unfriendly — Koreans don't read it as a flaw. For 'shy/timid' specifically, 소심하다 carries a more negative edge.
mistakes: Saying 내성적해요 — the stem is 내성적이다, so conjugate as 내성적이에요 / 내성적인
Confusing it with 소심하다 (timid/easily hurt); 내성적 is just inward-facing, not weak

usage: 외향적으로 + 변하다 = changed to be outgoing
examples: 우리 팀장님은 진짜 외향적이라서 회식 때 분위기를 다 살려요.
Our team lead is super outgoing, so they liven up the whole mood at company dinners.
분위기를 살리다 = liven up the mood; common at 회식
외향적인 사람은 모임에서 에너지를 얻는대요.
They say outgoing people get energy from gatherings.
-(ㄴ)대요 = reported speech (I heard that...)
저는 외향적이에요. 새 친구 사귀는 거 좋아해요.
I'm outgoing. I like making new friends.
친구를 사귀다 = make friends
nuance: 외향적이다 is the standard term for 'extroverted' and pairs naturally with MBTI talk, which is hugely popular in Korea — you'll constantly hear 'E야 I야?' (Are you an E or an I?). It's purely descriptive and positive-leaning. For 'energetic/lively' as a behavior rather than a trait, use 활발하다.
mistakes: Writing 외향적해요 — correct forms are 외향적이에요 / 외향적인
Mixing up 외향 (outward) with 외향성 — the adjective is 외향적이다, not 외향성이다

usage: 꼼꼼하게 = adverb form, very common with 확인하다
Often listed as a 장점 (strength) in interviews
꼼꼼히 = alternate adverb, slightly more written
examples: 계약서는 꼼꼼하게 읽어 보고 사인하세요.
Read the contract thoroughly before you sign.
Practical advice for 부동산/job contracts
저 사람 일 진짜 꼼꼼하게 해서 실수가 거의 없어.
That person works so meticulously they almost never make mistakes.
Casual praise; 실수 = mistake
면접에서 제 장점은 꼼꼼한 거라고 말했어요.
In the interview I said my strength is being detail-oriented.
장점 = strength; classic interview answer
nuance: 꼼꼼하다 is high praise in a work context — it means careful, thorough, and reliable with details, and it's one of the safest 'strengths' to claim in a Korean interview. Said about a person it's almost always a compliment. The flip side, when someone is so picky it slows things down, edges toward 까다롭다.
mistakes: Using it for being neat/clean — that's 깔끔하다, not 꼼꼼하다 (which is about thoroughness)
Forgetting the adverb: it's 꼼꼼하게 or 꼼꼼히, not 꼼꼼하게로

usage: Can be neutral or slightly negative
Also used for skin, allergies, stomach
examples: 시험 기간이라 요즘 좀 예민해. 미안.
It's exam season so I'm a bit on edge lately. Sorry.
Pre-emptive apology to a friend; very natural
저는 잠귀가 예민해서 작은 소리에도 깨요.
I'm a light sleeper, so even small sounds wake me up.
잠귀가 예민하다 = sensitive to sound while sleeping
그 얘기는 좀 예민한 주제라서 조심해서 말해야 해요.
That's a sensitive topic, so you have to speak carefully about it.
예민한 주제 = touchy subject
nuance: 예민하다 covers two things: a person being emotionally on-edge/touchy (often from stress), and physical sensitivity (skin, stomach, sleep). About someone's mood it can sound mildly critical, so people often say it about themselves to warn others. For a deeply sensitive, easily-hurt heart in a kinder sense, 섬세하다 sounds gentler.
mistakes: Confusing 예민하다 (sensitive/on-edge) with 민감하다 — they overlap, but 민감하다 is more common for issues/data being 'sensitive'
Don't use it to mean 'smart/sharp'; that's 예리하다

usage: He seems gruff on the outside
examples: 우리 아빠는 무뚝뚝하지만 속은 정말 따뜻해.
My dad is gruff but really warm on the inside.
Classic Korean description of fathers
사장님이 무뚝뚝하게 대답해서 화난 줄 알았어요.
The boss answered so curtly that I thought he was angry.
-(으)ㄴ 줄 알았다 = thought (mistakenly) that...
경상도 사람들은 무뚝뚝하다는 말을 자주 들어요.
People from Gyeongsang-do often get called blunt.
Common regional stereotype
nuance: 무뚝뚝하다 describes a curt, unexpressive manner — short answers, no small talk, a flat face — without necessarily meaning the person is mean. It's frequently paired with 'but warm inside' (속은 따뜻하다), especially about dads and older men. Don't confuse it with 차갑다 (cold-hearted), which implies actual coldness, not just a gruff style.
mistakes: Don't drop a syllable and write 무뚝하다 — the word doubles up: 무뚝뚝하다
Using it to mean 'rude'; it's about manner/affect, not 무례하다 (rude)

usage: High compliment for a partner or friend
has a warm way of speaking
다정다감 is a common four-syllable expansion
examples: 남자친구가 너무 다정해서 친구들이 다 부러워해요.
My boyfriend is so sweet that all my friends are jealous.
부러워하다 = be envious
선생님이 다정하게 말해 줘서 긴장이 풀렸어요.
The teacher spoke to me so warmly that my nerves eased.
긴장이 풀리다 = tension eases
그 카페 사장님은 항상 다정하셔.
The owner of that cafe is always so warm.
-(으)시- honorific for an older person
nuance: 다정하다 means warm, tender, and affectionate toward others — it's about emotional warmth and sweet treatment, a notch more intimate than 친절하다 (kind/polite, often to strangers or customers). It's a go-to compliment for partners, close friends, and warm teachers. The expanded form 다정다감하다 sounds slightly more literary but is common in praise.
mistakes: Using 다정하다 for polite service — staff being nice to customers is 친절하다, not 다정하다
Don't pair it with strangers oddly; 다정하다 implies real warmth, so it sounds off for a one-time formal interaction

usage: Mildly negative, but often said affectionately
까칠하게 굴다 = behave in a prickly way
examples: 우리 팀장님 평소엔 괜찮은데 마감 때만 까칠해져요.
Our team lead is usually fine but gets prickly only around deadlines.
마감 = deadline; -아/어지다 = become
왜 이렇게 까칠해? 무슨 일 있어?
Why are you so snippy? Is something wrong?
Casual concern between friends
그 사람 까칠해 보여도 알고 보면 착해.
He seems prickly, but once you really know him he's nice.
알고 보면 = when you actually get to know
nuance: 까칠하다 literally means 'rough to the touch' and figuratively describes someone snippy, easily irritated, or hard to please. It's lighter and more playful than calling someone outright mean — friends tease each other with it. Originally about texture (dry skin, stubble), so you may also hear 피부가 까칠하다 for rough skin.
mistakes: Using it as a serious insult — it's relatively mild; for genuinely mean use 못됐다
Confusing it with 까다롭다 (picky/demanding about standards); 까칠하다 is more about mood/attitude

usage: Encouraging a friend to speak up
Common joke phrase for small, harmless payback
examples: 저는 소심해서 식당에서 음식 바꿔 달라는 말도 잘 못해요.
I'm so timid I can't even ask to swap a dish at a restaurant.
Very relatable for newcomers nervous in Korean
소심하게 굴지 말고 그냥 물어봐!
Don't be timid, just ask!
Friendly push to be bolder
지각한 동료 자리에 몰래 포스트잇 붙였어. 소심한 복수지.
I secretly stuck a post-it on my late coworker's desk. Petty revenge.
소심한 복수 = classic playful expression
nuance: 소심하다 means timid, fainthearted, or easily intimidated — and unlike 내성적이다 (neutral 'introverted'), it leans negative, implying you hold back when you shouldn't. People often use it about themselves with a self-deprecating laugh. The set phrase 소심한 복수 ('petty revenge') is a beloved, very common joke.
mistakes: Treating 소심하다 as a synonym for 내성적이다 — introverts aren't necessarily timid; 소심 implies fear/holding back
Don't use it as a compliment in an interview; pick 신중하다 (prudent) instead

usage: take it easy, relax one's mind
examples: 저는 성격이 느긋해서 웬만한 일에는 스트레스를 안 받아요.
I'm laid-back, so most things don't stress me out.
웬만한 = most ordinary; 스트레스 받다 = get stressed
급할 거 없으니까 느긋하게 해.
There's no rush, so take your time.
급하다 = be in a hurry; reassuring tone
휴가 때는 느긋하게 늦잠도 자고 싶어요.
On vacation I want to sleep in and just take it easy.
늦잠 자다 = sleep in
nuance: 느긋하다 is the positive flavor of 'laid-back' — calm, unbothered, not easily rushed — and it pairs both with people's temperaments and with relaxed time (a 느긋한 아침). It contrasts with 급하다 (impatient/hasty). Note 여유롭다 overlaps but leans more toward 'having leeway/affluence of time or means,' while 느긋하다 is about temperament.
mistakes: Confusing it with 게으르다 (lazy) — 느긋하다 is unhurried by choice, not unwilling to work
Forgetting irregular-free conjugation: 느긋해요 / 느긋한, not 느긋어요

usage: Also describes a room or chat
examples: 새로 온 인턴이 성격이 활발해서 금방 다 친해졌어요.
The new intern is so lively that everyone got close fast.
금방 = quickly; 친해지다 = get close
동아리에서 활발하게 활동하면 친구를 많이 사귈 수 있어요.
If you're active in a club, you can make lots of friends.
동아리 = club; advice for newcomers
우리 반은 분위기가 활발해서 수업이 재미있어요.
Our class has a lively vibe, so lessons are fun.
분위기 = mood/atmosphere
nuance: 활발하다 describes lively, energetic, sociable behavior — it's how you'd praise someone who's bright and engaged in groups. It overlaps with 외향적이다 but describes observable liveliness rather than the inner extrovert trait, and it works for atmospheres and activities too (활발한 토론 = a lively debate). It's almost always a compliment.
mistakes: Using it as a pure synonym for 외향적이다 — 활발하다 is about visible energy, not the MBTI-style trait
Don't apply it to inanimate calm things; it implies motion/energy

examples: 급한 상황에서도 차분하게 대처해서 다들 놀랐어요.
Even in an urgent situation they handled it calmly, so everyone was impressed.
대처하다 = handle/respond to
차 한 잔 마시니까 마음이 좀 차분해졌어요.
After a cup of tea my mind calmed down a bit.
Natural cause-effect with -(으)니까
면접 때는 차분하게 대답하는 게 좋아요.
In interviews it's best to answer calmly.
Practical job advice
nuance: 차분하다 means calm, composed, and steady — a person who doesn't get rattled, or a quiet, settled mood. It's a strong compliment, especially for handling pressure, and it's a great trait to claim in interviews. It contrasts with 예민하다 (on-edge) and 급하다 (hasty); for a noisy place going quiet, you'd more likely use 조용하다.
mistakes: Confusing it with 조용하다 (quiet) — 차분하다 is about composure/temperament, not just low volume
Stem is 차분하다, so it's 차분해요 / 차분한, never 차분하해요

usage: Not caring much about details or others' moods
무심하게 = without thinking much of it
look after someone in a low-key way
Popular phrase: aloof on the surface, caring underneath
examples: 남편이 무심해서 제 머리 자른 것도 몰라요.
My husband is so inattentive he didn't even notice I cut my hair.
Extremely common relationship complaint
그 선배는 무심한 듯 챙겨 줘서 인기가 많아요.
That senior looks aloof but quietly looks out for people, so they're popular.
무심한 듯 챙기다 = the beloved 'cold but caring' type
친구가 무심하게 던진 말에 상처받았어요.
I got hurt by something my friend said offhandedly.
무심하게 던진 말 = a careless remark
nuance: 무심하다 means indifferent, aloof, or simply not paying attention to others' feelings and small changes — it's a frequent (half-joking) complaint about partners who don't notice anything. It isn't as harsh as 차갑다 (cold-hearted); a 무심한 person may care but just not show or notice. The trendy phrase 무심한 듯 챙기다 ('caring in a seemingly indifferent way') is a praised personality type.
mistakes: Confusing 무심하다 (inattentive/aloof) with 무관심하다 — 무관심하다 is stronger 'totally uninterested', often about topics
Don't equate it with 차갑다 (cold-hearted); 무심하다 is more about not noticing than being cold
